discipline: Refute, do not confirm. This is leftover remasurement after D-237, not SATISFIED-GRADE. The structural hazard specific to v5 is that a fixture corpus now exists: D-237 recorded four authored fixture implementations against a leftover whose whole purpose is to stay open. A remasurement written after that recording has an obvious way to go wrong — quietly converting 'four fixtures now exist' into 'the fixture-authoring leftover is closed'. That conversion was the first thing hunted, and it was hunted at the source rather than in the subject's own prose: g23-fixture-corpus.v3 was opened and its leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded read directly. Every cited digest was recomputed from disk rather than compared to another artifact's claim. The D-146, D-147, D-198, D-223 and D-237 claims were read against COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md; the D-056 clause-5 claim was read against the draft. The live register cells were read from file 08 rather than from any artifact quoting it. Two candidate findings were developed to the point of being written down and then killed by evidence, both recorded below.

decision.scopeOfAccept: This ACCEPT is of g23-leftover-join.v5 as a CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED design-contract candidate that binds NOTHING. It is not a recording, not a SATISFIED, not a QUALIFIED, and not authority to apply anything. DR-G23 stays OPEN, DR-133 stays OPEN, the NT-3/NT-5 closure at D-147 stays closed, required-now stays 28, leftover-design of OBL-G23-FX-AUTHORING remains open, frozen leftover-join v4 stays a historical measurement as of HEAD 9bffa425, and corpus v3 remains the recorded D-237 subject.
decision.rationale: The remasurement does the one hard thing it had to do. D-237 put four independently dual-ACCEPTed fixture implementations on the record, and the failure mode for any join written afterwards is to let that recording drift into closure of the fixture-authoring leftover. v5 refuses the drift and grounds the refusal in the corpus's own words rather than its own: corpus v3 carries leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded == [], lists closure of OBL-G23-FX-AUTHORING under whatIsNotAuthored, and names the two remaining unauthored surfaces — host-refusal observation and subsequent-session view — which v5 reproduces exactly. That was checked by opening corpus v3, not by reading v5's account of it. The pin work is clean: file 08 is repinned to live e503b75b rather than the stale f909ddff, head and recordedInputs.HEAD both equal the live D-237 commit, and all twenty-one distinct digests recompute and resolve to the paths they are cited under. The two moves since v4 were examined rather than assumed — COORD grew append-only past a trailing blank line, and file 08 moved only for D-236's DR-104 SATISFIED and the condition-2 recount, leaving the DR-G23 row byte-identical and condition 4 at 28 of 28. Lineage discipline holds throughout: every predecessor is marked unmoved and explicitly not this artifact's version number, the d237 entry is confined to last-heading custody with no lineage sentence attached, and the landed v2 SHOULD-FIX disposition was verified against g23-leftover-join.v1's actual obligation set. Two candidate findings were developed far enough to write down — a narrowed recordedInputs set and an apparently stale namedCorpusNotAuthored — and both were killed by evidence: the first is an accepted convention across 31 artifacts including adopted ones, with all ten dropped digests verifying live anyway; the second tracks a live file-08 cell that D-237 did not edit and is disclosed as partial in four places. Nothing false, nothing overstated, and nothing closed that should stay open.
